Framing Protocol v2

The framing protocol version two replaces the legacy length-prefixed format with a self-describing frame header. Every frame begins with a four-byte magic sequence followed by a variable-length header block encoded as canonical CBOR. Implementations MUST reject frames whose magic does not match, and SHOULD log the offending prefix for diagnostics.

The handshake starts when the client sends a HELLO frame containing its supported version range. The server answers with a WELCOME frame that pins the negotiated version. If the ranges do not intersect, the server closes the connection with a REJECT frame carrying a machine-readable reason code.

Flow control uses a credit scheme. Each side grants the peer an initial window of sixty-four frames, replenished in batches of sixteen as frames are consumed. Senders MUST NOT exceed the granted window; receivers MAY shrink the window by withholding grants but MUST NOT revoke credit already granted, because in-flight frames cannot be recalled.

Checksums are mandatory in version two. The trailer carries a CRC-32C over the header and payload. Frames failing the check are discarded silently and a NACK is scheduled on the next grant boundary, which keeps the hot path free of retransmission bookkeeping.
